title: 01 Composite and inverse functions: Visual Guide
outline: Title: 01 Composite and inverse functions: Visual Guide

1. Two Machines In Series | one input slider driving a single function (the taxi fare 3 + 2x) beside two functions wired end to end (minutes to temperature to cost), with the composite E(T(m)) = m + 20 computed live and the meaningless sum of the two formulas shown alongside | a composite feeds output into input and reads right to left, so its value is the outer quantity as a function of the inner variable - and in a linear model the fixed part is the value at zero, not the value at one

2. Which Function Last | three two-step processes (discount then tax, discount then a flat fee, Fahrenheit to Celsius to Kelvin) with both orders computed side by side and the gap between them measured | the outer function is whatever the story does last; composition is not commutative, agreement between two orders is a coincidence of pure scalings, and the inner function must produce what the outer one consumes

3. Substitute The Whole Thing | an oil spill with draggable growth rate k and time t, drawing the true circle A = k^2 pi t^2 against the circle you get by squaring only the t, with the substitution written out step by step | substitute the entire inner expression including its coefficient - squaring r = 4t gives 16 pi t^2, and leaving the 4 outside understates the area by exactly k at every instant

4. Horizontal Line Test | four rules (x^2, x^3, |x|, 2x-1) with a draggable horizontal line and five domain restrictions, counting intersections inside the kept domain and reading off the resulting inverse | invertible means one-to-one and nothing else; the horizontal line test draws it, and a restriction works only if it leaves no symmetric pair behind, which is why x >= 0 inverts x^2 to sqrt(x) while x != 0 and x <= 1 do not

5. The Round Trip | five candidate pairs pushed through both compositions from a test-value slider, plus f and g plotted with the mirror line y = x and the reflected point marked as landing on g or missing it | two functions are inverses only when f(g(x)) = x AND g(f(x)) = x on suitable domains - one direction can pass while the other fails, as it does for x^2 and sqrt(x) where g(f(x)) = |x|
